"According to the report, activity began to intensify in the early days of July and saw a notable increase following the public release of the Supreme Court’s ruling, which established legal precedent regarding the legal regime applicable to individuals entering Ceuta by sea. From that point on, a gradual increase in posts, videos, and messages related to the autonomous city was documented, with the campaign reaching its peak intensity in the days immediately preceding Morocco’s Throne Day celebrations.

Among the study’s key findings is the scale of activity achieved by the campaign. The research documents more than 11 million potential impressions, resulting from the aggregation of views of audiovisual content, members of digital communities, posts, comments, and interactions recorded during the analyzed period. For the report’s authors, this magnitude demonstrates the extraordinary reach achieved by the content disseminated across various platforms.

The analysis also reveals that the campaign did not follow a centralized structure. On the contrary, it identifies a distributed digital ecosystem in which different profiles assumed specific roles in content generation, viralization, redistribution, and logistical coordination." https://t.co/dTgWfJJ1th

It's been almost 2 months since I have cut down my screen time by 90%.

I no longer scroll social media, watch youtube, netflix, etc. No more video games.

I'm close to the happiest I've ever been. The only thing missing is the "work" or "productivity" element to my life atm. I am procrastinating a lot of things that have been on my to-do list for a long time.

A lot of emails and messages I need to respond to. A lot of admin work. A lot of community work. Some mistakes I made with yoshizen I need to figure out how to make up for. Tax stuff.

It's all piling up and I know I need to get to it soon but I cannot for the life of me find the motivation. I can't shake the dread I feel at the thought of sitting down at my computer for hours and hours.

It's funny. Being addicted to screens and dopamine is not a good thing, but removing them from my life, while overall a net positive, has also removed my ability to spend any time with the devices that rule our lives.

God damn it's hard to find balance.

Dunno if anyone out there has been through anything similar and come out the other side, but I am all ears for any tips or suggestions for re-finding purpose or motivation

tweets.text:
People who achieve success and drive progress deeply understand the cause-effect relationships that govern reality and have principles for using them to get what they want. The converse is also true: Idealists who are not well grounded in reality create problems, not progress.

What does a successful life look like? We all have our own deepseated needs, so we each have to decide for ourselves what success is. I don’t care whether you want to be a master of the universe, a couch potato, or anything else—I really don’t. Some people want to change the world and others want to operate in simple harmony with it and savor life. Neither is better. Each of us needs to decide what we value most and choose the paths we take to achieve it.
#principleoftheday
